Fever, foul-smelling discharge and pain across the lower belly — it may be pelvic inflammatory disease
Pain that suddenly gets worse **in a way that's different from your usual period pain**, or so bad you can't move even after a painkiller
clinic: Missing school or work every month for 3–6 months or more even with proper use of anti-inflammatory painkillers
Pelvic pain on non-period days, or pain during sex
Periods suddenly much heavier, or with clots
Severe period pain that started after age 25
With fever or foul-smelling discharge
pharmacy: Lower belly or back pain mostly on the first 1–2 days of your period
Pain you can manage with medicine and a warm pack
dysmenorrhea.escalate: See a doctor if **you can't get through the day even with medicine**, if your periods suddenly get heavier, or if your lower belly keeps hurting outside your period. Endometriosis and fibroids need to be checked.

headache.name: Headache
er: A thunderclap headache that peaks within seconds to 1 minute
With fever, stiff neck, drowsiness or confusion
Weakness in an arm or leg, slurred speech, vision problems or a seizure
Headache and vomiting that get worse after a blow to the head
Eye pain + red eye + blurred vision (acute glaucoma)
Severe headache from week 20 of pregnancy or within a few weeks after birth, with blurred or flashing vision, or sudden swelling of the face or hands (preeclampsia — **go to the emergency room now**)
clinic: Headaches on 4 or more days a month, or painkillers on 10 or more days
A headache starting for the first time after age 50
Headaches that feel different from usual and keep getting worse
Headaches set off by coughing, straining or exercise
Headaches that get much worse when lying down or standing up
A new headache during pregnancy
History of cancer, AIDS or a weakened immune system
pharmacy: Tension headache or migraine like your usual ones
Headache after poor sleep, stress or heavy drinking that responds to painkillers
headache.escalate: If you have headaches **four or more days a month** or take **painkillers ten or more days a month**, come in — it's time to change your medicine. A headache that hits like a thunderclap means the emergency room right away.

toothache.name: Toothache and pain after a tooth is pulled
toothache.short: Getting by until you see the dentist
er: Swelling spreading to the eye or neck, with trouble swallowing or breathing
High fever + can't open your mouth
**If your lower jaw hurts along with chest tightness or a numb left arm, call 119 now** — heart trouble can feel like a toothache
Swelling under the jaw and a feeling that your tongue is being pushed up
clinic: Swollen cheek or gums, pus, or fever
Not controlled by painkillers for 3 days or more
Pain getting worse on day 3–4 after a tooth is pulled
pharmacy: Getting by for 1–3 days until your dental appointment
Expected pain after a tooth is pulled
toothache.escalate: Come in right away if **your cheek or gums are swollen with pus or fever**. Also if painkillers don't control it for more than three days, or if pain gets worse from the third day after a tooth is pulled.

sorethroat.name: Sore throat
er: Drooling because you can't swallow, trouble breathing, or a muffled voice (epiglottitis or abscess)
Can't open your mouth + severe swelling on one side
Still hard to swallow after three days, with a fever staying near 39°C
A sore throat with a **gurgling or harsh sound** when breathing, or you need to sit and lean your head forward to breathe comfortably
clinic: High fever of 38.5°C or more + white pus on the tonsils
Severe pain for more than 3 days
Ear pain or swollen glands under the jaw
With a rash
pharmacy: Sore throat with runny nose and cough (a cold)
Within 3 days, no fever or a mild fever
sorethroat.escalate: Come in if you have **a fever over 38.5°C and white pus on your tonsils**. Also if it's severe for more than three days, or your ear hurts and the area under your jaw swells. Not being able to swallow your saliva and feeling short of breath is an emergency.

cold.name: Cold (runny nose, cough, body aches)
cold.short: Why a combination cold medicine isn't the answer
er: Short of breath with bluish lips
Confusion or a seizure
Chest pain, or blood in your phlegm
clinic: Fever lasting more than 3 days
Lasting more than 10 days, or getting better then worse again
Ear pain, face pain (sinusitis), or yellow phlegm + fever
High fever and muscle aches during flu season (antiviral medicine within 48 hours)
A cold in someone with asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, pregnancy, age 65 or older, or a baby or young child
pharmacy: Runny nose, sneezing, mild fever and aches, within 3 days
Still eating and staying active
cold.escalate: Come in if **the fever lasts more than three days**, if you get yellow phlegm or face pain, or if you're short of breath. Whether you need antibiotics is decided at the visit.

fever.name: When you have a fever
fever.short: Choosing a fever reducer for adults and children
er: A baby under 3 months old with a temperature of 38°C or higher
Seizure, hard to wake or less alert, or going limp
Stiff neck, severe headache, or purple spots that don't fade when pressed
Short of breath or bluish lips
40°C or higher + no response to fever reducers
38.0°C or higher during cancer treatment or while taking medicine that weakens the immune system — don't wait with a fever reducer; call your treating hospital right away or go to the emergency room
clinic: Fever lasting more than 3 days
A baby 3–6 months old with a temperature of 38°C or higher
With ear, throat or urinary pain
With a rash
People with chronic illness, age 65 or older, or pregnant
pharmacy: 38–39°C with a cold, within 3 days, drinking well and active
fever.escalate: Come in right away if the fever lasts **more than three days**, **a baby under 3 months has 38°C**, or there's a stiff neck or a seizure.
find: how to bring down a fever

cough.name: Cough and phlegm
cough.short: Dry and wet coughs need different medicines
er: So short of breath you can't finish a sentence, bluish lips
Coughing up a lot of blood
Sudden chest pain + trouble breathing
clinic: Cough for 3 weeks or more
Yellow phlegm + fever, chest pain
Wheezing or night-time cough (possible asthma)
Weight loss, night sweats, or blood in phlegm
A dry cough that started after taking a blood pressure medicine (ACE inhibitor)
pharmacy: Cough with a cold, less than 3 weeks
No fever or a mild fever, not short of breath
cough.escalate: Come in if the cough lasts **more than 3 weeks**, if you have yellow phlegm with fever or chest pain, or if you wheeze and it's worse at night. If there's blood, come right away.

rhinitis.name: Stuffy nose, runny nose, sneezing
er: Severe swelling around the face or eyes + high fever (orbital cellulitis)
Severe headache + stiff neck
Bloody discharge from **only one side** of the nose for weeks
A child with foul-smelling discharge from only one nostril — something may be stuck inside
clinic: Rhinitis that comes back every year (prescription sprays, testing)
Yellow discharge for more than 10 days + face pain or fever (sinusitis)
Blocked on one side only, nosebleeds, or bad smell
Snoring or mouth breathing during sleep in a child
pharmacy: Clear runny nose, sneezing and itching, seasonal
Nose symptoms with a cold, within 1 week
rhinitis.escalate: **If it comes back every year**, a prescription spray works much better. Yellow discharge for more than ten days or face pain may be sinusitis; one-sided blockage with nosebleeds needs its own check.

heartburn.name: Heartburn and acid reflux
er: Black stools or vomiting blood
Squeezing chest pain, cold sweat, numb left arm (rule out the heart)
Severe belly pain + a hard belly
clinic: Lasting or coming back for 2 weeks or more
New or long-lasting symptoms after age 40 (national stomach cancer screening also starts at 40)
Food sticking or pain when swallowing, weight loss, anemia
Heartburn while taking anti-inflammatory painkillers or aspirin long-term
pharmacy: Heartburn after meals or late-night eating, within 2 weeks
Responds to medicine
heartburn.escalate: Come in if you need medicine for **more than 2 weeks**, it's hard to swallow, you're losing weight, or your stools are black. You'll need an endoscopy.

dyspepsia.name: Indigestion and bloating
dyspepsia.short: When digestive aids work and when they don't
er: Upper belly pain + cold sweat, shortness of breath, numb left arm (heart attack)
A hard belly that hurts more when you press and let go
Vomiting blood or black stools
Upper-right belly pain with fever and chills, or yellow eyes or skin (cholangitis)
Upper belly pain spreading to the back, getting worse, with vomiting (pancreatitis)
clinic: Coming back for 2 weeks or more
Weight loss, anemia or black stools
Upper-right belly pain + worse after fatty food (gallbladder)
New or long-lasting after age 40 (national stomach cancer screening also starts at 40)
pharmacy: Bloating after overeating, a day or two
dyspepsia.escalate: Come in if **it keeps coming back for more than 2 weeks**, you're losing weight, or your stools are black. Upper-right belly pain after fatty food points to the gallbladder.

diarrhea.name: Diarrhea
diarrhea.short: Diarrhea you shouldn't stop with medicine
er: Hardly any urine, or too dizzy to stand (severe dehydration)
Severe belly pain that's hard to bear (this alone is enough)
Bloody stools together with a high fever
A baby or young child who is limp with no tears or urine
clinic: Lasting 2 days or more, or 6 or more times a day
Fever of 38°C or higher; bloody, black or mucus-filled stools
Diarrhea after travel, or while taking antibiotics
Diarrhea in babies, older adults, pregnancy or chronic illness
pharmacy: Watery diarrhea without fever or blood, within 2 days, able to drink
diarrhea.escalate: **If you have a fever or blood in your stool**, don't take anti-diarrhea medicine — come in right away. **If you're dizzy and your mouth is very dry**, you're dehydrated and IV fluids can help. Also if it's no better after two days.

constipation.name: Constipation
er: Severe belly pain + vomiting + swollen belly + no gas or stool at all (bowel obstruction)
Suddenly no stool or gas at all, with a tight belly and vomiting — your bowel may be blocked
Red blood in your stool, or black, sticky stool
clinic: Lasting 2 weeks or more
New after age 50, lasting 6 weeks or more
Blood in stool, weight loss or anemia
Thinner stools, or constipation alternating with diarrhea
pharmacy: Short-term constipation (travel, change in diet)
No belly pain or vomiting
constipation.escalate: If it's no better after **2 weeks**, started new after age 50, or comes with blood in the stool, weight loss or anemia, your bowel needs to be checked.

motion.name: Motion sickness
er: Sudden severe dizziness + slurred speech, double vision or weakness on one side (rule out stroke)
Dizziness with weakness in an arm or leg on one side or slurred speech — call 119 now
Sudden hearing loss in one ear with dizziness — see an ear, nose and throat doctor the same day; hearing may not come back if you wait
clinic: Repeated dizziness or vomiting not related to travel
With ringing in the ears or hearing loss
pharmacy: Nausea only while traveling
motion.escalate: See a doctor if you're dizzy and vomiting **when you're not traveling**, or if ringing in the ears or hearing loss comes with it.

allergy.name: Allergies, hives and itching
allergy.short: Choosing an antihistamine that won't make you drowsy
er: Swelling of lips, tongue or eyes, tight throat, hoarse voice
Shortness of breath or wheezing, dizziness or fainting (anaphylaxis)
Hives + sudden belly pain or vomiting
clinic: Coming back for 6 weeks or more
Hives all over the body that continue despite medicine
Rash with fever or joint pain
Happens again and again after a certain food or medicine
pharmacy: Hives or itching in one area, insect bites
Responds to medicine, no breathing symptoms
allergy.escalate: Come in if **it keeps coming back for more than 6 weeks** or hives all over your body continue despite medicine. **If your lips or eyes swell and you're short of breath**, call 119 now.

wound.name: Cuts, scrapes and burns
wound.short: What to do before any ointment
er: Bleeding that doesn't stop after 10 minutes of pressure
Deep burn (white or black skin, no pain); electrical or chemical burn; possible airway burn
Large cut on the face, or an object stuck deep in the skin
clinic: Gaping wound (needs stitches, within 6–8 hours)
Animal or human bite, rusty nail
Pus, spreading redness or fever
A 2nd-degree burn larger than your palm; burns on the face, hands, joints or genitals
A wound in someone with diabetes or a weakened immune system
pharmacy: Shallow scrape or cut, 1st-degree burn no bigger than a coin
Bleeding stops with pressure
wound.escalate: **A gaping wound needs stitches within 6–8 hours.** Come in right away for an animal or human bite, a rusty nail, or pus or fever.

mouth.name: Mouth ulcers and sores
er: Dehydrated because you can't eat or drink
Mouth so swollen it's hard to breathe
**A sore in one spot that hasn't healed after 2 weeks** — be sure to see a doctor
Mouth sores together with sores or blisters on the eyes or genitals
clinic: Lasting 2 weeks or more, or coming back often
Large or many, with fever or swollen glands
With eye or genital ulcers
White coating (thrush) or repeated lip blisters
pharmacy: 1–2 small ulcers, within 2 weeks
mouth.escalate: Come in if it hasn't healed after **more than 2 weeks**, if there are large or many sores with fever, or if ulcers also appear on the eyes or genitals.

insomnia.name: When you can't sleep
insomnia.short: How many days for sleep aids
er: Thoughts of hurting yourself — suicide prevention line 109 (24 hours)
Thoughts of wanting to die — 109 (24 hours, no call charge)
Family has seen you stop breathing in your sleep, or you wake with headaches and doze off while driving
clinic: 3 or more nights a week, for 3 weeks or more
Severe daytime sleepiness or poor focus
Snoring or pauses in breathing
With depression or anxiety
pharmacy: Short-term sleeplessness (jet lag, stress), a few days
insomnia.escalate: Come in if you can't sleep **three or more nights a week for more than 3 weeks**. Be sure to come if you've been told you snore heavily or stop breathing in your sleep.

dryeye.name: Dry, tired eyes
er: Sudden loss of vision or part of your vision
Eye pain + headache + vomiting (acute glaucoma)
Chemical splash (rinse under running water for 15 minutes, then go to the emergency room)
clinic: Lasting 2 weeks or more
Pain, blurred vision, or halos around lights
Pus-like discharge or swollen eyelids
pharmacy: Gritty, tired eyes after screen use
dryeye.escalate: Come in if it's the same after **more than 2 weeks**, or if it hurts, your vision blurs, or you see halos around lights. Pus-like discharge with swollen eyelids is a different problem.

hangover.name: Hangover
er: Vomiting blood or black stools
Confusion or a seizure
Chest pain or irregular heartbeat
clinic: Vomiting or dehydration lasting more than 24 hours
Severe upper belly pain (pancreatitis or gastritis)
Frequent binge drinking (talk about alcohol use)
pharmacy: Headache and nausea that get better within a day
hangover.escalate: Come in if **you're still vomiting after a day** or the upper belly hurts badly. If you binge drink often, it's fine to talk about that too.

nausea.name: Nausea and feeling like vomiting
nausea.short: Fluids first, then find the cause
er: Vomiting blood or something that looks like coffee grounds
Severe belly pain with a hard belly, or pain in the lower right belly
Nausea with chest tightness or a cold sweat — especially in older adults or people with diabetes
Severe headache, stiff neck, or confusion
Unable to keep even water down for more than a day, with hardly any urine
clinic: Lasting more than two days
When you could be pregnant
Started after a new medicine
Coming back for weeks with weight loss
pharmacy: The cause is likely (indigestion, motion sickness, hangover) and you can drink fluids
nausea.escalate: **If you vomit blood or something like coffee grounds, your belly is very painful and hard, or you have chest tightness with a cold sweat**, go to the emergency room right away.

dandruff.name: Dandruff and itchy, flaky scalp (seborrheic dermatitis)
er: Scalp swelling with pus and fever that is spreading
clinic: No change after 4 weeks
Thick white patches on the scalp, or similar patches on elbows or knees (possible psoriasis)
Lots of oozing or crusts, or hair falling out
Spreading over the whole face
Yellow crusts on a baby's scalp
pharmacy: White flakes and itching on the scalp
dandruff.escalate: **If your scalp swells with pus and fever and it's spreading**, see a doctor right away.

wart.name: Warts (bumpy growths on hands or feet)
wart.short: Salicylic acid for weeks; freezing if that fails
er: The treated area turns red and swollen, feels hot, oozes pus and is spreading
clinic: On the face or genitals
No change after several weeks, or spreading to several spots
You have diabetes or take medicine that weakens the immune system
Not sure whether it's a corn or a wart
Mixed colors, changing shape, or bleeding
pharmacy: A small wart on the hand or foot and no diabetes
wart.escalate: **Something with mixed colors, an irregular changing shape, or bleeding** may not be a wart — have a skin doctor check it.

arthritis.name: Knee and hand arthritis
er: One joint suddenly red, swollen and hot, with fever (septic arthritis or gout)
After an injury, the joint feels out of place and you can't put weight on it
Joint pain together with **a rash all over and a high fever**
Joint pain with sudden weight loss or drenching night sweats
clinic: Morning stiffness for 1 hour or more, with pain in several joints on both sides (rule out rheumatoid arthritis)
Pain wakes you at night
You can walk noticeably shorter distances
Fluid often builds up in the knee
No change after 2–4 weeks of medicine
pharmacy: Long-standing joint pain that hurts with movement and eases with rest
Morning stiffness under 30 minutes
No swelling or warmth
arthritis.escalate: If **morning stiffness lasts more than an hour** or several joints hurt on both sides, rheumatoid arthritis needs to be checked. Also if pain wakes you at night or you can't walk as far.

gout.name: Gout (a joint suddenly red and swollen)
gout.short: Sudden pain in the big toe, ankle or knee
er: Swollen, painful joint with a fever of 38°C or higher (rule out septic arthritis)
Several joints suddenly swollen at once and you can't move
**If a rash breaks out all over after starting a gout medicine (allopurinol), stop it right away and see a doctor** — it's a rare but dangerous allergic reaction
An attack that hasn't settled after more than 2 weeks, or a joint starting to change shape
clinic: A first attack (you need a diagnosis — it must be told apart from a bacterial infection). If you also have a fever, go the same day
No change after 3 days
Attacks twice or more within 1 year
Kidney problems make anti-inflammatory painkillers hard to use
Lumps (tophi) you can feel
pharmacy: Diagnosed with gout before, and the attack is like your usual ones
One painful joint and no fever
Getting better within a day or two
gout.escalate: **A first attack needs a diagnosis** — it must be told apart from germs in the joint (septic arthritis), **especially if you have a fever**. If it's the same after three days or happens more than twice within 1 year, it's time to start a medicine that lowers uric acid.

cramp.name: Leg cramps
cramp.short: When your calf knots up at night
er: Only one calf swollen, hot and painful (possible deep vein thrombosis)
Sudden weakness and loss of feeling in a leg
**If your urine turns dark like cola after a cramp, see a doctor right away** — muscle breakdown can strain the kidneys
Not a cramp, but **calf pain every time you walk that goes away with rest, again and again** — your blood vessels need to be checked
clinic: Happening every night so you can't sleep
Calf pain when walking during the day that eases with rest
With numbness or loss of feeling in hands or feet
Started around the time of a new medicine
pharmacy: Occasional calf cramps at night that ease within a few minutes
Happening in either leg, taking turns
No swelling or color change
cramp.escalate: **Calf pain when walking during the day that eases with rest** may be a blood vessel problem. Also come in if you have numbness in your hands or feet, or can't sleep every night.

hemorrhoid.name: Hemorrhoids (piles)
er: Heavy bleeding, dripping blood, with dizziness or pale skin
Severe swelling around the anus with fever and you can't sit (possible abscess)
**Black or tar-like sticky stool** may not be hemorrhoids but bleeding from higher up — you need to see a doctor
Bowel habits changed for weeks (thinner stools, diarrhea and constipation taking turns) or weight loss
clinic: Bleeding continues after 1–2 weeks of medicine
The lump has to be pushed back in by hand, or won't go back
New bleeding after age 50, thinner stools, or weight loss
Hemorrhoids during pregnancy
pharmacy: Bright red blood on toilet paper after a bowel movement
Anal pain and itching, but you can walk
The lump goes back in on its own
hemorrhoid.escalate: Come in if **bleeding continues after 1–2 weeks of medicine**, or if the lump has to be pushed back by hand. New bleeding after age 50, thinner stools or weight loss means your bowel needs to be checked.

athletes-foot.name: Athlete's foot and toenail fungus
er: Foot red, swollen, hot and with a fever (cellulitis)
Diabetes with a wound on the foot that smells
**If a red streak runs up the top of the foot or toward the calf**, see a doctor right away — the infection is spreading
No change, or spreading, after more than 4 weeks of antifungal cream
clinic: No change after 4 weeks of cream
Several toenails thick and discolored
You have diabetes or a weakened immune system
Spread to the fingernails
pharmacy: Soggy, itchy skin between the toes
White peeling on the soles
No swelling, warmth or pain
athletes-foot.escalate: Come in if **it's the same after 4 weeks of cream**, or several toenails get thick. **If you have diabetes**, foot wounds are risky, so come early.

shingles.name: Possible shingles
shingles.short: A band of blisters on one side
er: Blisters around the eye or on the tip of the nose (can threaten vision)
Blisters around the ear with facial weakness or dizziness (Ramsay Hunt syndrome)
A widespread rash in someone with weak immunity (cancer treatment, transplant, long-term steroids)
Severe headache, stiff neck or change in alertness
clinic: A band of blisters on one side of the body
Burning or tingling in that spot before the blisters
Within 72 hours of the rash (the sooner the better)
Pain that stays after the rash has healed
pharmacy: None — if you think it's shingles, go to a clinic right away
shingles.escalate: If you see **a band of blisters on one side of your body**, come in that day. Burning or tingling in the spot before blisters is also a sign. **Around the eye or ear** is an emergency.

bite.name: Insect, mosquito and tick bites
bite.short: When you've been bitten or stung
er: Shortness of breath, a tight throat, or a hoarse voice
Swelling of the face, lips or tongue
Hives spreading all over with dizziness or feeling faint
Stung by many bees
High fever with bleeding gums or nose, or confusion
clinic: Bitten by a tick, or found one attached
Fever within 1–2 weeks after being outdoors
A black scab at the bite
Redness still spreading after a day
Pus, warmth or pain getting worse
The bite hasn't healed after more than a week
pharmacy: Only redness and itching where a mosquito or bug bit
Swelling smaller than your palm
No fever and feeling well
bite.escalate: Come in if **a tick was attached to you**, you get a fever within 1–2 weeks after being outdoors, or a **black scab** forms at the bite. If you're short of breath and your face swells, call 119.

dizziness.name: Dizziness
er: Slurred speech or weakness in an arm or leg on one side
Seeing double or losing half of your vision
With the worst headache of your life
Can't stand or walk on your own
Chest pain or fainting
clinic: Repeated spinning dizziness (rule out BPPV or Ménière's disease)
With a blocked ear, ringing or hearing loss
Started around the time of a new medicine
Lightheaded every time you stand up (orthostatic hypotension)
You've fallen because of dizziness
pharmacy: Brief dizziness like motion sickness that settles quickly
Only a few seconds when changing position
No other nerve symptoms
dizziness.escalate: **Slurred speech, weakness in an arm or leg on one side, seeing double, or not being able to walk on your own — call 119 now.** Even without those signs, **if severe dizziness you've never had before lasts several hours, see a doctor that day** — strokes with “only dizziness” really happen.

stye.name: Stye and swollen eyelid
stye.short: When the eyelid is swollen and sore
er: Swelling spreading to the face with fever (orbital cellulitis)
Pain when moving the eye, or the eye feels like it's bulging
Blurred vision or seeing double
clinic: A lump still there after 1–2 weeks
Keeps coming back
Lots of discharge and both eyes red (rule out pink eye)
You have diabetes or a weakened immune system
pharmacy: Only the eyelid edge is swollen and sore
Normal vision and the eye itself doesn't hurt
No fever
stye.escalate: Come in if **a lump is still there after 1–2 weeks** or it keeps coming back. If the whole eyelid swells and you have a fever, come right away.

gastroenteritis.name: Stomach bug (vomiting and diarrhea)
er: Vomiting so much you can't keep water down
No urine for half a day or more, or too dizzy to stand
Drowsy and slow to respond
Severe belly pain in one spot that hurts more when you press and let go
Vomiting blood
clinic: Lasting more than two days, or diarrhea 6 or more times a day
Fever over 38°C
Bloody or black stools
Older adults, babies, or people with weak immunity
Diarrhea that started after recent antibiotics
Diarrhea after travel abroad
pharmacy: Vomiting and diarrhea without fever or blood
Able to keep down at least small sips of water
Passing urine and not dizzy
Within two days
gastroenteritis.escalate: **If you haven't passed urine for more than half a day, are dizzy with a very dry mouth, or can't even keep water down**, come in right away. You need IV fluids. Older adults and babies can get worse within a day.

uti.name: Bladder infection (painful urination)
er: Fever of 38°C or higher with flank or lower back pain (kidney infection)
Vomiting so you can't keep water down
Severe shaking chills and confusion (possible sepsis)
No urine at all
clinic: Frequent, burning urination and feeling you haven't emptied
Blood in the urine
Pregnant or could be pregnant
Painful urination in a man
Coming back more than three times within 1 year
pharmacy: Hardly ever — if you think it's a bladder infection, the rule is to see a doctor
uti.escalate: If you **need to go often, it burns, and you feel you haven't emptied**, a doctor's visit is the answer. **If your side hurts and you have a fever**, it has reached the kidneys — come right away. Definitely if you're pregnant.
find: feel like I still need to pee

conjunctivitis.name: Pink eye (red eye, discharge)
er: Eye pain and worse vision
Strong sensitivity to light
Severe redness and pain in a contact lens wearer
Swelling around the eye with fever (orbital cellulitis)
Chemical in the eye — rinse under running water for 20 minutes right away, then go to the emergency room
clinic: Lots of thick yellow discharge, severe
No change after a week
Itching that comes back every season
You have diabetes or a weakened immune system
A child who can't open their eyes
pharmacy: Only redness and discharge, normal vision
The eye itself doesn't hurt
Not especially sensitive to light
conjunctivitis.escalate: **Lots of thick yellow discharge** needs antibiotic eye drops. If it hurts, your vision drops, or light bothers you, come right away.

nosebleed.name: Nosebleed
er: Doesn't stop after more than 20 minutes of pressure
Blood keeps running down the back of your throat so you swallow it
Dizzy, pale and in a cold sweat
Nosebleed after a face injury
Trouble breathing
clinic: Often happens again on one side
You take a blood thinner
Gum bleeding or easy bruising too
A lump inside the nose, or one side stays blocked
pharmacy: Stops within 5–10 minutes of pressure
Not much blood and no dizziness
Only now and then when the air is dry
nosebleed.escalate: Come in if it **doesn't stop after pressing 5–10 minutes two or three times, more than 20 minutes in all**, or keeps happening on one side. Definitely if you take a blood thinner or also bleed from the gums or bruise easily.

frozen-shoulder.name: Can't raise your arm (frozen shoulder, rotator cuff)
frozen-shoulder.short: Hard to lift the arm, pain at night
er: After a fall you can't lift the arm at all and the shoulder looks different (dislocation or fracture)
Shoulder red, swollen and hot with fever (infection)
Sudden weakness and loss of feeling in the arm
Shoulder or arm pain with chest tightness, shortness of breath or a cold sweat, or that gets worse when walking or climbing stairs and eases with rest — it may be your heart. **Call 119 now**
clinic: Arm weakness so you drop things, or can't hold your arm up once raised
The arm won't go up even with someone's help
No better after more than 6 weeks
Pain keeps you awake at night
Stiff shoulder in someone with diabetes
Numbness running from the neck down the arm
pharmacy: Shoulder pain and stiffness that came on slowly
Worse at night but no fever
No injury
frozen-shoulder.escalate: Come in if **your arm won't go up even with help**, it's the same after more than 6 weeks, or pain keeps you awake at night.

incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence (leaking urine)
incontinence.short: Leaks when coughing, or hard to hold it
er: Not a drop of urine all day and a tight lower belly
Leaking urine with leg weakness or numbness around the anus (spinal cord problem — same day)
With high fever or flank pain
clinic: Leaking has made you go out less
Started suddenly or getting worse fast
Blood in urine, or pain
Incontinence in a man
No change after 3 months of exercises
pharmacy: Only advice on pads or adult diapers — there's no treatment medicine at the pharmacy
incontinence.escalate: **If it's keeping you from going out**, that alone is a reason to see a doctor. Definitely if it started suddenly, is getting worse fast, or there's blood in your urine.

bph.name: Weak urine flow (enlarged prostate)
bph.short: Weak stream, waking often at night
er: No urine at all with a tight, painful lower belly (sudden blockage — same day)
Painful urination with high fever and chills (prostate or kidney infection)
Clots of blood in the urine
clinic: Weak stream and waiting before it starts
Waking two or more times a night
Ongoing feeling of not emptying
No better on medicine
pharmacy: None — an enlarged prostate needs a prescription
bph.escalate: **If no urine comes out at all and your lower belly is tight**, come that same day. A weak stream and waking two or more times a night can get better with treatment.
find: getting up at night to pee

osteoporosis.name: Osteoporosis (weak bones)
osteoporosis.short: More dangerous because it doesn't hurt
er: After a fall, groin or hip pain so you can't put weight on the leg (hip fracture)
Sudden severe back pain and you can't straighten up (spinal compression fracture)
Leg weakness or loss of bladder or bowel control
clinic: Women 65 and older, men 70 and older — get a bone density test at least once
You've lost 3 cm or more in height
A bone broke from a minor fall
Taking steroids for 3 months or more
Early menopause, or a parent who had a hip fracture
pharmacy: Advice on vitamin D and calcium only — there are no treatment medicines at the pharmacy
osteoporosis.escalate: **Women over 65 and men over 70** should have a bone density test at least once. Definitely if you've lost more than 3 cm in height or broke a bone in a minor fall.

sprain.name: Sprained ankle and bruises
er: Can't put any weight on it
The foot looks odd or a bone seems to stick out
Toes change color or lose feeling
clinic: Swelling and pain the same after 3–5 days
Pain when pressing the back of the ankle bone, the inner bone on top of the foot, or the bone at the base of the little toe
Couldn't take 4 steps right after the injury and still can't
pharmacy: Twisted and swollen
sprain.escalate: **If you couldn't take four steps right after the injury and still can't**, the bone needs to be checked. Also come in if it hurts to press behind the ankle bone, or it's the same after 3–5 days.

tendon.name: Wrist and elbow tendinitis, tennis elbow
tendon.short: Outer elbow or thumb-side wrist aches when gripping or twisting
er: Swelling and an odd-looking wrist after an injury
Red, swollen and hot, and you can't move your fingers
Fingers change color or lose feeling
Weak hand or fingers so you drop things
clinic: The same after more than 6 weeks
Numb or weak hand
Pain wakes you at night
Pain that started suddenly after an injury
pharmacy: Outer elbow or thumb-side wrist aches when gripping or twisting
tendon.escalate: Come in if it's the same after **more than 6 weeks**, your hand is numb or weak, or pain wakes you at night.

plantar.name: Plantar fasciitis and heel pain
plantar.short: Sharp heel pain with your first steps in the morning
er: A **snap** at the time of injury and you can't put weight on it (fascia or Achilles tear)
Heel swollen, hot, with fever (infection or gout)
Pain that continues even at rest at night, with swelling or weight loss
Numbness or loss of feeling in the foot
A foot wound when you have diabetes
clinic: The same after 6–12 weeks of stretching and insoles
Pain at rest or at night
Both heels hurt, with morning stiffness in the low back or hips, or eyes that often turn red (possible spinal arthritis)
Foot swelling, warmth or numbness
pharmacy: Sharp heel pain with your first steps in the morning
plantar.escalate: Come in if **it's the same after 6–12 weeks**, it hurts at rest or at night, or both heels hurt.

coldsore.name: Cold sores
coldsore.short: Tingling at the edge of the lip, then blisters
er: Red, painful eye or blurred vision (corneal infection)
Spreading widely across the face, or fever and swollen glands under the jaw
Blisters spreading over the body in someone with eczema
People with weak immunity (cancer treatment, transplant, AIDS), or contact with a newborn
A child with sores all over the inside of the mouth who can't eat or drink
clinic: Not healed after more than 2 weeks
In 1 year, it comes back more than 6 times
Pain around the eye or a red eye
Weak immunity or severe eczema
pharmacy: Tingling at the edge of the lip, then blisters
coldsore.escalate: **If the area around your eye hurts or your eye turns red, come right away** (the cornea can be damaged). Also if it hasn't healed after more than 2 weeks or comes back more than six times within 1 year.

eczema.name: Eczema and atopic itch
eczema.short: Dry, red, itchy skin on inner arms, neck and hands
er: Skin red and peeling all over, with fever and chills
Clusters of small blisters on eczema with oozing and fever (eczema herpeticum — especially in children)
Spreading yellow crusts or pus with fever
Swelling of the face or lips and shortness of breath
A child with fever who is limp
clinic: No change after 1 week of pharmacy steroid cream
Oozing, yellow crusts, or suddenly worse (bacterial infection)
Painful clusters of small blisters (herpes)
Itching keeps you from sleeping night after night
pharmacy: Dry, red, itchy skin on inner arms, neck and hands
eczema.escalate: Come in if it's the same **after 1 week of pharmacy steroid cream**, if oozing or yellow crusts appear, or if painful clusters of small blisters break out.

acne.name: Acne
acne.short: Red pimples and small bumps keep coming on the forehead and chin
er: Suddenly many swollen, hot boils on the face or body with body aches
clinic: No change after 8–12 weeks of pharmacy products
Red lumps, cysts or scars starting (early prescription prevents scars)
Worse around the chin and mouth before every period
So bothered it weighs on your mind
Acne with irregular periods, extra hair growth or rapid weight change
Started after a medicine such as steroids, lithium or testosterone
Sudden severe acne as an adult
pharmacy: Red pimples and small bumps keep coming on the forehead and chin
acne.escalate: Come in early if it's the same **after 8–12 weeks of pharmacy products**, red lumps or cysts appear, or **scars start to form**. Scars are hard to reverse once they form.

vaginitis.name: Vaginal itching and discharge
er: Fever, lower belly pain or pain during sex (pelvic inflammatory disease)
Bleeding that isn't your period
Change in discharge during pregnancy
Severe swelling of the vulva with blisters or sores
Possible exposure to a sexually transmitted infection
clinic: First time having these symptoms
No change after 3 days of vaginal tablets, or not healed after 7 days
Gray, thin, fishy-smelling discharge, or yellow and frothy (not a yeast infection)
Pregnancy or diabetes, or in 1 year it comes back more than 4 times
pharmacy: Itchy, with more white discharge
vaginitis.escalate: **If it's your first time**, or the discharge is gray, thin and fishy-smelling, or yellow and frothy, it isn't a yeast infection. If you have a fever or lower belly pain, come right away.

pms.name: Premenstrual syndrome (PMS)
pms.short: Bloated, irritable, headache and back pain for a few days before your period
er: Thoughts of wanting to die before your period (suicide prevention line 109 — call now)
Depression or anxiety that continues regardless of your period
Severe headache before your period with vision changes or numbness
Sudden swelling and shortness of breath
Your cycle itself breaking down (very heavy or irregular bleeding)
clinic: No change after two or three cycles of pharmacy medicine
Irritability or low mood shaking your daily life or relationships
Symptoms don't ease even after your period starts
Severe pain not controlled by painkillers
pharmacy: Bloated, irritable, headache and back pain for a few days before your period
pms.escalate: Come in if it's the same **after two or three cycles of pharmacy medicine**, or irritability and low mood are shaking your daily life and relationships. If it doesn't ease once your period starts, it may be something else.

meno.name: Menopause symptoms
meno.short: Hot flushes, poor sleep, more irritable
er: Bleeding again after menopause (no period for 1 year)
A breast lump or nipple discharge
Sudden chest pain, shortness of breath, or swelling of one leg (especially while taking hormones)
Severe heat with weight loss and a pounding heart (thyroid)
Severe depression or thoughts of wanting to die (suicide prevention line 109 — call now)
clinic: Hot flushes or poor sleep making daily life hard — don't wait 4 weeks
No change after 4 weeks of pharmacy products
Vaginal dryness, painful sex, or repeated bladder infections
Bleeding again after menopause
pharmacy: Hot flushes, poor sleep, more irritable
meno.escalate: **If hot flushes or poor sleep make daily life hard, don't wait 4 weeks.** Come right away if you bleed again after menopause or feel a breast lump.

fatigue.name: Tiredness and low energy
fatigue.short: Tired and weak for weeks even after sleeping
er: Tiredness with unexplained weight loss and night sweats or fever
Shortness of breath, chest pain or a pounding heart
Pale with black stools or very heavy periods (anemia)
With severe thirst and lots of urination
Tiredness with thoughts of wanting to die (suicide prevention line 109 — call now)
With yellow skin or eyes, or leg swelling
clinic: Lasting more than 4 weeks even with enough sleep
Weight loss, fever, drenching night sweats or shortness of breath
Severe tiredness that started suddenly
Low mood and loss of interest
pharmacy: Tired and weak for weeks even after sleeping
fatigue.escalate: Come in if it lasts **more than 4 weeks even with enough sleep**. Don't wait if you're losing weight, soaking the sheets with sweat at night, or short of breath.

drymouth.name: Dry mouth
drymouth.short: Mouth very dry, waking at night for water
er: Severe thirst and frequent urination with vomiting, weakness or confusion (very high blood sugar emergency)
Swollen, painful salivary gland with fever (salivary gland infection)
Mouth sores so you can't eat or drink
clinic: Still dry 2–4 weeks after changing medicines (find the cause)
Also dry eyes, or swollen painful joints (check for Sjögren's syndrome)
Thirst with frequent urination and weight loss (check for diabetes)
Hard to swallow, or mouth sores
pharmacy: Mouth very dry, waking at night for water
drymouth.escalate: Come in if **it's still dry 2–4 weeks after changing medicines**, your eyes are also dry and joints hurt, or you're thirsty, urinating often and losing weight.

gumdisease.name: Swollen, bleeding gums
gumdisease.short: Gums bleed when brushing and feel loose
er: Swelling down to the cheek or under the jaw with fever, and hard to open your mouth (deep infection — same day)
Gum bleeding that won't stop (taking a blood thinner, or a blood disorder)
White or red patches on the gums that stay for more than 2 weeks (check for mouth cancer)
Several teeth suddenly loose
clinic: Still bleeding after 2 weeks of flossing and interdental brushes
Loose teeth or receding gums
No change after 1 month of gum medicine
Bad breath or pus
pharmacy: Gums bleed when brushing and feel loose
gumdisease.escalate: See a dentist if **your gums still bleed after 2 weeks of flossing and interdental brushes**, or your teeth are loose or gums are receding. If your cheek swells and you can't open your mouth, go that same day.

ibs.name: Frequent belly pain with changing bowel habits
ibs.short: Belly pain for months with diarrhea and constipation taking turns
er: Blood in stool or black stools
Losing weight without dieting
Belly pain that wakes you at night
Belly pain with fever and vomiting
Told you have anemia, or dizzy and pale
clinic: Weight loss or blood in stool — don't wait
Belly pain wakes you at night
Started new after age 50
Still struggling after 2–4 weeks of diet changes and antispasmodics
pharmacy: Belly pain for months with diarrhea and constipation taking turns
ibs.escalate: **Don't wait if you're losing weight or there's blood in your stool.** Belly pain that wakes you at night or starts new after age 50 also means your bowel needs to be checked.

burn.name: Burns
burn.short: Red, stinging skin from boiling water, oil or an iron
er: A burn larger than 3 adult palms or 2 of a child's palms
White or leathery burn that **doesn't hurt** (deep burn that reached the nerves)
Burn to the face or neck, or hoarse voice and shortness of breath after breathing smoke
Electrical or chemical burns (even if the skin looks fine)
Widespread blisters in a child or someone 65 or older
clinic: A burn larger than your palm
Face, hands, feet, joints or genitals
Not healed after more than 2 weeks
Yellow, smelly ooze (infection)
pharmacy: Red, stinging skin from boiling water, oil or an iron
burn.escalate: Come in if it's **larger than three adult palms or two of a child's**, or on the face, hands, feet, joints or genitals even if small. A white or leathery burn that doesn't hurt is deeper.

numbness.name: Numb, tingling hands or feet
numbness.short: Tingling fingertips and toes, worse at night
er: Sudden weakness in an arm or leg on one side, or slurred speech (stroke — 119)
Both legs quickly getting weak, and you can't urinate or urine leaks (cauda equina syndrome — same day)
Numbness with a cold, pale, painful leg (blocked blood vessel)
Numbness and weakness after a back injury
A foot wound that doesn't hurt and is oozing (diabetic foot)
clinic: Lasting more than 2 weeks
Numb hands wake you at night (carpal tunnel)
You have diabetes
Weakness or unsteady walking — don't wait
pharmacy: Tingling fingertips and toes, worse at night
numbness.escalate: **Sudden weakness in an arm or leg on one side or slurred speech means 119.** If it lasts more than 2 weeks or you have diabetes, see a doctor.

anxiety.name: Anxiety and tension (pounding heart)
er: Squeezing chest pain with a cold sweat (check the heart first)
Nearly fainted or fainted after a pounding heart
Breathing fast with tingling lips and stiff hands
Thoughts of wanting to die — call the **suicide prevention line 109** now
Hearing or seeing things others don't
clinic: Repeated attacks where you can't catch your breath
Anxiety is wrecking your work, going out or sleep
Anxiety or restlessness lasting more than a month
Hard to fall asleep without alcohol or pills
Repeated pounding with an irregular pulse, or a heartbeat that suddenly races then stops (get a heart tracing)
pharmacy: Tense and unable to sleep for a few days
anxiety.escalate: See a doctor if **attacks where you can't breathe and feel you're dying** keep happening, or anxiety is wrecking your daily life. If there's chest pain too, check the heart first.

earwax.name: Blocked ear and muffled hearing (earwax)
er: **Sudden hearing loss in one ear — see an ear, nose and throat doctor that day.** Sudden hearing loss may not come back if you wait
Pus or blood from the ear with a fever
Dizziness and vomiting after an ear injury
clinic: No change after 5 days of ear drops
You wear a hearing aid and sounds have become quieter
Ringing in the ear (tinnitus) or dizziness
A child who keeps touching their ear and is fussy
pharmacy: Ear feels blocked and full but doesn't hurt
Blocked feeling after using hearing aids or earphones
earwax.escalate: **If it hurts, pus or blood comes out, or your hearing drops suddenly**, it may not be earwax. If it's the same after three or four days of drops, it's better to have it removed at a clinic.

tinnitus.name: Ringing in the ears (tinnitus)
tinnitus.short: A ringing sound in your ear
er: **Sudden hearing loss in one ear with ringing — see an ear, nose and throat doctor that day.** Sudden hearing loss needs quick treatment to recover
**If you hear a thumping in time with your heartbeat**, see a doctor — it may be a blood vessel problem
Ringing with weakness in one side of the face or an arm or leg, or slurred speech — call 119 now
clinic: Lasting more than a month
With trouble hearing
You can't sleep or your mood is low
Started after a head injury
pharmacy: In both ears, hearing is fine, and it's been the same for weeks
tinnitus.escalate: **Sudden hearing loss in one ear with ringing — go to an ear, nose and throat doctor that day.** With sudden hearing loss, time decides recovery. A thumping sound in time with your pulse also needs a doctor.

deworm.name: Deworming medicine (pinworm, roundworm)
er: Severe belly pain and vomiting with no stool or gas — worms may be blocking the bowel
Yellow eyes and dark urine after taking the medicine
If hives break out all over or you're short of breath, stop the medicine and see a doctor
**If you took it while pregnant or possibly pregnant**, be sure to tell your doctor
clinic: Still itchy after two doses
A baby under age two
Pregnant or breastfeeding
You often eat raw freshwater fish and have frequent belly pain — liver flukes need a different medicine
pharmacy: A child scratching the anus at night and sleeping poorly
The whole family taking one dose as prevention
deworm.escalate: **If the itching is still there after two doses**, it's likely not worms. If you have severe belly pain or vomiting, or you're pregnant, don't take it yourself — see a doctor.

smoking.name: When you want to quit smoking
smoking.short: How not to go it alone
er: Squeezing chest pain or shortness of breath
Thoughts of harming yourself while taking a quit-smoking medicine — call **109** (suicide prevention) or **119** right away
clinic: You've failed several times with nicotine aids
Quitting while taking heart, diabetes or mental health medicines
Pregnant or planning a pregnancy
Your mood drops a lot while on a quit-smoking medicine
pharmacy: You've decided to quit and are choosing patches or gum
Trying to quit by cutting down first
smoking.escalate: If **your mood drops a lot or dark thoughts come** while on a quit-smoking medicine, stop it and see a doctor right away. **Squeezing chest pain** means 119.

hairloss.name: Hair loss
er: Scalp red, swollen and hot, spreading with fever and chills
clinic: A round bald patch appears suddenly (alopecia areata)
A lot of hair falls out all over at once
Itchy scalp with dandruff, oozing or crusts
Eyebrow or body hair falling out too
Tired, sensitive to cold and gaining weight — possible thyroid problem
A woman with irregular periods, acne and more body hair
pharmacy: The crown or forehead slowly thinning over several years
hairloss.escalate: See a skin doctor if hair falls out **in a round patch suddenly**, **all over at once**, or if there's **oozing, crusts or scarring on the scalp**.

corn.name: Corns and calluses (sharp pain on the sole)
er: Red, swollen, hot, with pus and spreading
In someone with diabetes, a foot wound turning black or smelling
Fever with a swollen, painful foot
clinic: Corns or calluses in someone with diabetes or circulation problems
No change after several weeks, or keep coming back
Not sure whether it's a corn or a wart
Painful enough to change how you walk
pharmacy: No diabetes, and one hard spot that hurts when pressed
corn.escalate: **A foot wound in someone with diabetes, a red swollen spot with pus, or a spot turning black** needs a doctor right away.

bp.title: If you take blood pressure medicine
bp.short: Missed doses · care with pharmacy medicines · why medicines change
bp.lead: Blood pressure medicine keeps your blood pressure down while you take it. Good readings usually mean **the medicine is working**.
do: Take it **at the same time every day**. Morning or evening, as your doctor decided.
Even when your readings are good, **don't stop on your own.** Lowering or stopping is decided with your doctor.

Measuring at home morning and evening makes it easier to adjust your medicine at visits. If the **average over several days** measured correctly at home is a top number of **135 or more** or a bottom number of **85 or more** (mmHg), have it checked at a visit.
When you buy painkillers or cold medicine at a pharmacy, first say **“I take blood pressure medicine.”**
er: **If an arm or leg on one side suddenly gets weak or your speech slurs, whatever your blood pressure → call 119 now.** The same goes for severe chest pain or shortness of breath.
If your lips, tongue or throat swell or you can't breathe → **call 119 now**
If your blood pressure is a top number of **180 or more** or a bottom number of **110 or more** (mmHg) with a severe headache or blurred vision → **call 119 now**

If, with no symptoms, the top number is **180 or more** or the bottom number **110 or more** → rest 5 minutes and measure again. If it stays high, **contact your prescriber and be seen today**. (110 is a cautious cutoff chosen by this app)
If you feel faint and like you'll fall when standing up, or actually fainted → be seen today
bp.miss: Take it as soon as you remember. If it's almost time for your next dose, take just that one, and **don't take two doses at once.** Be especially careful not to miss medicines ending in -olol for several days — stopping suddenly can bring on chest pain.

dm.title: If you take diabetes medicine
dm.short: Low blood sugar · sick days · before contrast scans
dm.lead: Each type of diabetes medicine has its own cautions. You can tell the type from **the last letters** of the ingredient name on your medicine bag.
do: Don't skip meals, and take your medicine at the set times. **Medicines ending in -mepiride or -clazide** can cause low blood sugar if you don't eat.

If low blood sugar comes on (cold sweat, shakiness, pounding heart, feeling foggy) and you're alert and able to swallow, take **15–20 g of sugar** (for juice, check the sugar amount on the nutrition label) and **check again 15 minutes later.** If it's still **below 70 mg/dL**, take the same amount once more. If you don't get better or become confused, get help right away.
On days you can't eat because of heavy vomiting or diarrhea, ask your doctor or pharmacist **what to do with metformin or -gliflozin medicines** — sometimes you need to pause them.
Before a test that uses contrast dye (such as a CT scan), be sure to say **that you take metformin**.
er: If low blood sugar makes someone **confused or unable to swallow**, put nothing in their mouth → **call 119 now**
If blood sugar stays **over 300 mg/dL** with vomiting, shortness of breath or extreme weakness → **emergency room**
dm.miss: What to do for a missed dose **depends on the medicine** (take glimepiride just before a meal and don't skip that meal). If it's almost time for your next dose, skip it — **taking two doses at once can cause low blood sugar**. Ask ahead of time what to do with medicines that can cause low blood sugar on days you can't eat.

chol.title: If you take cholesterol medicine (-statins)
chol.short: Muscle pain · liver tests · why medicines change
chol.lead: Cholesterol medicine is taken **long-term** to lower the chance of blocked blood vessels (heart attack, stroke).
do: At the same time every day. **Take simvastatin in the evening**; atorvastatin, rosuvastatin and pitavastatin can be taken any time.
Even when your numbers become normal, **don't stop on your own** — that's thanks to the medicine.
If your muscles are **severely** painful and weak and **your urine is dark like cola**, stop the medicine and see a doctor right away.
er: Severe muscle pain and weakness with **dark brown urine** → **emergency room today**
Yellow eyes or skin, or dark urine with upper-right belly pain → **see a doctor right away**
chol.miss: Take it when you remember, but if your next dose is within 12 hours, skip it. **Don't take two doses at once.**

thy.title: If you take thyroid medicine (levothyroxine)
thy.short: Empty stomach in the morning · 4 hours apart · when to get blood tests
thy.lead: This medicine replaces thyroid hormone your body lacks. The dose is tiny (micrograms), so **how you take it changes how well it works.**
do: Take it **in the morning on an empty stomach with water** and eat 30 minutes to 1 hour later. The Korean label only says “1 time per 1 day” (once daily) without a set time — the empty-stomach advice comes from the US label and clinic practice. Taking it at the same time every day matters most.
Keep calcium, iron, magnesium and antacids **4 hours apart.**
After a dose change, it's adjusted with **a blood test 6–8 weeks later**.
**If you find out you're pregnant, tell your doctor right away** — the dose often needs to go up.
er: Chest pain → **call 119 now**
Pounding heart, shaky hands, heavy sweating and trouble sleeping → the dose may be too high, **see a doctor soon**
thy.miss: Take it as soon as you remember, and skip it if your next dose is close. It stays in the body a long time, so missing one day won't upset things much, but **if you miss doses often**, tell your doctor.

mind.title: If you take sleep, anxiety or depression medicine
mind.short: Medicines not to mix · stopping · actions while half-asleep
mind.lead: Medicines for sleep and mood **add up drowsiness when combined, and cause trouble if stopped suddenly.** Following just these two points keeps most people safe.
do: Take sleeping pills **right after you lie down**, and only when you can sleep 7–8 hours.
**Don't take them with alcohol** — your breathing can become shallow and you can fall more easily.
**Don't combine them** with pharmacy sleep aids (diphenhydramine, doxylamine), motion sickness medicine or nighttime cold medicine — the drowsiness adds up.
**Don't suddenly stop** a medicine you've taken a long time; taper slowly with your doctor.
er: Shallow breathing and hard to wake → **call 119 now**
Thoughts of wanting to die, or sudden worse anxiety or restlessness after starting or changing a medicine → contact your doctor right away. In an emergency, **109** (suicide prevention) · **119**
mind.miss: If you remember a sleeping pill late at night, **skip it that night** — you may be drowsy until morning. For daily depression or anxiety medicines, follow the product's instructions, but if your next dose is close, skip it and **don't take a double dose or make it up with a short gap.**

blood.title: If you take blood thinners
blood.short: Bleeding signs · care with pharmacy medicines · before procedures
blood.lead: These medicines prevent clots that block blood vessels (stroke, heart attack). Because bleeding may not stop easily, **adding a new medicine and the time before a procedure** matter most.
do: Take it at the same time every day. **Don't stop on your own** — stopping suddenly raises the risk of stroke, heart attack or a blocked stent.
Before dental work, an endoscopy or surgery, **be sure to say you take this medicine.** Your prescriber decides when to pause it (the clopidogrel label says 5–7 days before surgery).
When buying a painkiller at a pharmacy, choose **acetaminophen** first. Anti-inflammatory painkillers and cold medicines with aspirin increase bleeding.
With warfarin you have regular **blood-thinness tests**. If you start or stop a new medicine or supplement, the next test is moved up.
er: Vomiting blood or something like coffee grounds, or stools that are **black or bloody** → **go to the emergency room now**
**If you hit your head**, even if you feel fine → emergency room today — bleeding can start later
Sudden weakness in an arm or leg on one side, slurred speech, or a severe headache → **call 119 now**
blood.miss: **It depends on the medicine.** For dabigatran, **skip it if your next dose is less than 6 hours away.** Take warfarin only if you remember the same day. In the period at the start of clot treatment when you take **rivaroxaban 15 mg twice a day**, the label has different rules (up to 2 tablets at once may be allowed) — ask your pharmacist right away then. With any of these, you **never take two doses at once**.

bone.title: If you take osteoporosis medicine (-dronates)
bone.short: Empty stomach in the morning · a full glass of plain water · stay upright 30 minutes · tell your dentist
bone.lead: This medicine slows bone loss to **reduce fractures**. Taking it the right way lets it be absorbed and protects your esophagus.
do: Most should be taken **as soon as you get up, on an empty stomach, with a full glass of plain water (about 200 mL)**. Milk, coffee, juice or mineral water stop it being absorbed. But some products, such as delayed-release risedronate, **are taken differently** — follow the product's instructions on your medicine bag first.
With alendronate, **don't lie down for at least 30 minutes and until you've eaten breakfast.** With ibandronate, stay upright for **at least 60 minutes** and hold off on food and other medicines.
Take calcium and vitamin D too, but **after waiting following this medicine**.
Before having a tooth pulled or an implant, **tell your dentist you take this medicine.** Good daily brushing and regular checkups lower the chance of rare jawbone problems.
er: If you **vomit blood or have black, sticky stools** → **go to the emergency room now**. If you're dizzy or feel faint, call **119**.
Pain when swallowing or burning behind the breastbone → stop the medicine and **see a doctor soon** (esophagus injury)
If **new pain starts** in your thigh or groin → be sure to mention it at your visit (an early sign of a rare thighbone fracture)
bone.miss: If you forget your **once-a-week** tablet, take one **the morning after you remember**, then go back to your usual day. Never two on the same day. For a **once-a-month** tablet (ibandronate), if your next dose is more than 7 days away take it the next morning; if it's within 7 days, skip it.

gi.title: If you take acid reducers (-prazoles, -prazans)
gi.short: Before meals · don't stop on your own · every 1 year ask if you still need it
gi.lead: These lower stomach acid to **heal stomach ulcers and reflux**, and **protect the stomach** while you take anti-inflammatory painkillers or blood thinners.
do: Many -prazole medicines are taken **before breakfast** (usually 30 minutes to 1 hour before). Dexlansoprazole and -prazan medicines like tegoprazan can be taken with or without food — follow **the product's instructions on your medicine bag**.
If it was prescribed along with a blood thinner or anti-inflammatory painkiller, **don't stop on your own even when you feel better** — it's there to prevent stomach bleeding.
If you've taken it a long time, **about every 1 year ask at your visit, “Do I still need this?”** If not, you may be able to cut down or stop.
For a few days to a few weeks after stopping, **heartburn may briefly get worse** (acid rebounds). It usually passes.
er: If you **vomit blood or have black, sticky stools** → **go to the emergency room now**. If you're dizzy or feel faint, call **119**.
Food not going down well, weight loss, or ongoing vomiting → **see a doctor soon** (you may need an endoscopy)
gi.miss: Take it as soon as you remember, and skip it if your next dose is close. Don't take two doses at once.

resp.title: If you use an inhaler (asthma, COPD)
resp.short: Daily vs rescue inhalers · rinse your mouth · check your technique
resp.lead: With inhalers, **technique is half the effect**. There are **daily inhalers, rescue inhalers for when you're short of breath, and ones that do both** — check which kind you were prescribed.
do: **If you were told to use an inhaler daily, use it every day even when you feel better** — it keeps airway inflammation down. Some prescriptions use the same inhaler daily and for breathlessness (budesonide–formoterol), so follow the action plan you were given.
After using an inhaler with a steroid, **rinse your mouth with water and spit** (prevents mouth thrush and hoarseness).
Breathe all the way out, then seal your lips and breathe in. **Ask the pharmacy or clinic to show you once**, and bring your inhaler to visits.

With asthma, using **a reliever like albuterol** for symptoms **more than twice a week** (not counting before exercise) is a sign it isn't controlled — mention it at your visit. For other inhalers, follow your action plan.
er: If even after the rescue inhaler you're **too short of breath to finish a sentence**, your lips turn blue, or you're drowsy and limp → **call 119 now**

If your rescue inhaler **wears off quickly so you need it again soon, or you're getting more breathless** → don't wait, **see a doctor right away**. If you can't finish a sentence or you're limp, **call 119 now**.
resp.miss: If you forget your daily inhaler, use it as soon as you remember, and skip it if the next dose is close. Don't use two doses at once.

pros.title: If you take prostate medicine (-osins, -sterides)
pros.short: Stand up slowly at first · tell your eye doctor before cataract surgery · effects take months
pros.lead: There are medicines that ease urine flow (-osins) and **medicines that shrink the prostate (-sterides)**. Some people take both.
do: Tamsulosin is usually prescribed **once a day**, and silodosin **once or twice a day** — follow the number of doses and after-meal instructions on your medicine bag. **In the first few days or when the dose goes up you may feel dizzy when standing** — get up slowly.
**Before cataract surgery, tell your eye doctor you take this medicine** — the iris can flutter during surgery.
-steride medicines take **months (usually 6 months)** to work. They roughly halve your prostate blood test number, so **tell them at testing that you take this medicine.**
If a -steride tablet is broken, **don't let a woman who is or could become pregnant touch it**.
er: If **no urine comes out at all** and your lower belly is swollen and painful → **go to the emergency room now** (the urine needs to be drained)
If **blood keeps showing** in your urine → **see a doctor soon**
pros.miss: Take it that day if you remember, but skip it if it's the next day. Never a double dose. If you restart an -osin after a few days off, you may feel dizzy like at the start.

gout.title: If you take gout medicine (allopurinol, febuxostat, colchicine)
gout.short: Uric acid medicine every day · don't stop during an attack · stop right away if you get a rash
gout.lead: Medicine that lowers uric acid is taken **every day to prevent attacks**; colchicine is used **during attacks or to prevent attacks in the first few months**.
do: Take uric-acid-lowering medicine (allopurinol, febuxostat) **every day even when nothing hurts.** **Don't stop** even if an attack comes.

If you take **azathioprine or mercaptopurine** (immune-suppressing or blood cancer medicines), **be sure to tell your doctor before** starting gout medicine — together they can cause serious blood problems.
Attacks can actually happen in the first few months, so some people also take **a medicine like colchicine for 3–6 months**.
The dose is adjusted bit by bit with blood tests, aiming for **uric acid below 6 mg/dL**.
Drink plenty of water, and cut down on alcohol (especially beer) and sugary drinks.
er: If a **new rash** appears after taking allopurinol → stop the medicine and **contact your prescriber right away**. With fever, blisters, mouth sores or face swelling → **go to the emergency room now**
If after colchicine you have **severe diarrhea or vomiting with muscle pain or weakness** → stop the medicine and **see a doctor soon**
gout.miss: Take it as soon as you remember, and skip it if your next dose is close. Never a double dose.

blad.title: If you take bladder medicine (-fenacin, mirabegron)
blad.short: Takes weeks to work · dry mouth and constipation · watch memory in older adults
blad.lead: This medicine eases urgent, frequent urination (overactive bladder). **It takes a few weeks to feel the effect.**
do: Take it once a day at the same time. **It can take 4–8 weeks to help** — don't stop after a week.
Medicines like -fenacins often cause **dry mouth and constipation**. Sip water often, and mention it at your visit if constipation is bad.
In people 65 and older, medicines like -fenacins can cause **fogginess or memory loss**. If family notices a change, please mention it at the visit.

Mirabegron **can raise blood pressure.** It shouldn't be used if blood pressure isn't controlled below a top number of **180** or a bottom number of **110** — check your blood pressure before and while taking it.
er: If **no urine comes out at all** and your lower belly is swollen and painful → **go to the emergency room now**
Sudden eye pain and redness with poor vision → **go to the emergency room now** (acute glaucoma)
blad.miss: If your next dose is close, skip it — never a double dose. For mirabegron and others, check **the missed-dose instructions on your medicine bag or leaflet**.

ster.title: If you take steroid pills (prednisolone, methylprednisolone)
ster.short: Morning after food · don't stop suddenly after long use · blood sugar, sleep, bones
ster.lead: This medicine strongly calms inflammation and the immune system. **Short courses are usually safe**, but after long use you need to taper it properly.
do: Take it **after breakfast**. Taking it in the evening can keep you awake.
If you've taken it **more than 3 weeks**, **don't stop suddenly** — taper bit by bit as your doctor decides.
While taking it, **blood sugar can rise**, you may sleep less, and you may feel restless or irritable. If you have diabetes, check your blood sugar more often.
If you take it **more than 3 months**, bones can weaken, so discuss bone tests, calcium and vitamin D.
er: **Black stools or vomiting blood** → **call 119 now**
Fever or a worsening infection → **see a doctor soon** (signs of infection can be hidden by the medicine)

After lowering or stopping a steroid you took a long time, if you're **extremely weak, dizzy, or keep vomiting** → **go to the emergency room now**. If you faint or become confused, call **119**. Also contact a doctor right away if vomiting stops you from taking the medicine.
ster.miss: For a once-a-day medicine, take it that day if you remember, but skip it if it's the next day. Never a double dose.

dem.title: If you take dementia medicine (donepezil, memantine)
dem.short: Same time every day · stomach upset at first · tell us if your pulse slows · avoid drowsy medicines
dem.lead: This medicine **slightly slows** the decline of memory. It doesn't cure, so keep taking it **steadily** even if you don't feel better.
do: Take it **at the same time every day**. Donepezil is usually taken in the evening; if you have lots of dreams or wake up, ask whether you can switch to mornings.
At first or when the dose goes up, you may get **nausea, diarrhea or loss of appetite**. It usually gets better within a few weeks.
**If your pulse slows, or you feel dizzy or faint**, be sure to mention it at your visit.
**Drowsy cold medicines, sleep aids and motion sickness medicines** work against this medicine and can worsen memory — tell the pharmacy you take dementia medicine.
er: **Fainting or passing out** → **call 119 now**
**Black stools or vomiting blood** → **call 119 now** (especially if you've had a stomach ulcer or also take anti-inflammatory painkillers)
dem.miss: If you miss a day, skip it and take it as usual the next day. Never a double dose. **Each dementia medicine restarts differently** — if you've been off the rivastigmine patch **for more than 3 days**, don't go straight back to the old dose; check first. For tablets too, if you've been off **more than a week**, ask whether to restart from the starting dose.

eye.title: If you use glaucoma eye drops
eye.short: Same time every day · 5 minutes apart for two drops · press the inner corner
eye.lead: These drops lower eye pressure to **keep the optic nerve from more damage**. Often you use them **every day for life**, even though nothing hurts.
do: Use them **at the same time every day**. Drops like latanoprost are usually once in the evening.
After putting them in, **close your eye and gently press the inner corner (near the nose) for 1–2 minutes** — the drop stays in the eye longer and less gets into the body.
If you use two kinds of drops, **wait more than 5 minutes between them** so the first one isn't washed out.
Don't let the bottle tip touch your eye or lashes. Take contact lenses out and put them back 15 minutes after the drops.
er: **Sudden severe eye pain and redness, blurred vision, headache and vomiting** → **go to the emergency room now** (acute glaucoma)
If after timolol you get **new shortness of breath or wheezing** → don't use more and **see a doctor right away**. If you're very short of breath or can't finish a sentence, call **119**.
eye.miss: It depends on the drop. **With latanoprost, don't add extra for a missed dose — use one at the next scheduled time.** For other drops check the product's instructions, and don't use a double dose.

park.title: If you take Parkinson's medicine
park.short: Keep to the times · don't stop suddenly · stand up slowly · watch for urges and sleepiness
park.lead: These medicines replace dopamine to **reduce tremor, stiffness and slowness**. The effect rises and falls over time, so **the time you take them** matters.
do: Take them **at the set times**. If there are times the effect wears off, note when and bring it to your visit.
Levodopa **may be absorbed less when taken with protein like meat or eggs**. If the effect is uneven, discuss meal timing and spacing.
**Don't stop suddenly or cut down a lot** — a dangerous reaction with stiffness and fever can happen.
You may feel dizzy when standing — **get up slowly.**
er: **High fever with severe stiffness and confusion** → **call 119 now**
**A fall with injury, or fainting** → see a doctor right away
park.miss: Take it as soon as you remember, and skip it if your next dose is close. Never a double dose.

pain.title: If you take prescription painkillers (anti-inflammatories, tramadol, nerve pain medicine)
pain.short: Don't double up with pharmacy painkillers · drowsiness and dizziness · no alcohol
pain.lead: Prescription painkillers **easily overlap with pharmacy painkillers.** Avoiding overlap matters most.
do: While taking a prescription anti-inflammatory (-profen, -fenac, -coxib), **don't add a pharmacy anti-inflammatory (ibuprofen, naproxen, dexibuprofen)** — they're the same family.
Take anti-inflammatory painkillers **after meals**. People 65 and older or who've had a stomach ulcer often get a stomach-protecting medicine with them.
Tramadol, gabapentin and pregabalin cause **drowsiness and dizziness**. Avoid driving for the first few days, and **don't drink alcohol.**
**Don't suddenly stop** nerve pain medicines (gabapentin, pregabalin); taper with your doctor.
er: **Black stools or vomiting blood** → **call 119 now**
**Shallow breathing and hard to wake** → **call 119 now** (when tramadol or nerve pain medicine is combined with sleeping pills or alcohol)
Chest pain or weakness in an arm or leg on one side → **call 119 now**
pain.miss: If it's an as-needed medicine, you can skip it. If you take it at set times, take it as soon as you remember, skip it if the next dose is close, and never a double dose.

abx.title: If you take prescription antibiotics or antifungals
abx.short: For the set number of days · don't stop on your own · what each one must avoid
abx.lead: Take antibiotics **for as long as your doctor set**. Each medicine has **different things you shouldn't take with it**.
do: Take them **at the set times and for the set number of days**. If you feel better and want to finish early, **don't stop on your own** — ask your prescriber.

The gap between -floxacin medicines and **antacids, calcium, iron or magnesium** depends on the antibiotic and which you take first (ciprofloxacin: this medicine 2 hours before or 6 hours after) — check **the gap on the leaflet for your medicine**.
With metronidazole, **don't drink alcohol while taking it and for 3 days after** — it causes severe vomiting and flushing.
-mycin and -conazole medicines **often clash with other medicines** — tell them every medicine you take (colchicine, some cholesterol medicines and others).
er: **Swelling of the lips, tongue or throat, or trouble breathing** → **call 119 now**
**Watery diarrhea several times a day** that keeps going, or with blood → **see a doctor soon** (colitis after antibiotics)
**A rash or blisters all over with fever** → stop the medicine and **go to the emergency room now**
abx.miss: Take it as soon as you remember, and skip it if your next dose is close. Never a double dose.

derm.title: If you take oral skin medicine (isotretinoin, -cyclines)
derm.short: No pregnancy at all on isotretinoin · -cyclines with a glass of water, stay upright · watch the sun
derm.lead: Oral acne medicines work well but **come with clear rules**. Above all, isotretinoin **must never overlap with pregnancy.**
do: If you could become pregnant and take isotretinoin, follow the birth control your prescriber advised **from at least one month before starting, while taking it, and for one month after stopping**. You also need **the required pregnancy tests** before and during treatment. It causes severe birth defects.
While taking isotretinoin and for one month after stopping, **don't donate blood.** Also avoid vitamin A supplements.
Take -cycline medicines **with a full glass of water, and don't lie down for 30 minutes** — they can cause sores in the esophagus. Keep them **2–3 hours** apart from calcium, iron, antacids and milk.
Both make your **skin burn easily in the sun** — use sunscreen. If your lips or skin get dry, moisturize often.
er: If you **find out you're pregnant** while on isotretinoin → stop it right away and **contact your prescriber today**
**If your mood drops badly or you have thoughts of wanting to die** → stop the medicine and get help right away (suicide prevention 109)

**Isotretinoin must not be taken with doxycycline or minocycline.** If you get a severe headache with blurred vision or vomiting, stop the medicine and **get emergency care right away** (raised pressure in the head).
derm.miss: Take it as soon as you remember, and skip it if your next dose is close. Never a double dose.

herb.title: If you take herbal medicine or herbal granules
herb.short: Always mention them with other medicines · licorice and ephedra · check if taken long-term
herb.lead: Pharmacy herbal granules (such as galgeun-tang [kakkonto], socheongryong-tang and jakyakgamcho-tang) and decoctions from a Korean medicine clinic are **medicines** too. If you take them with prescription medicines, **tell both sides**.
do: **Tell your clinic and pharmacy you take herbal medicine.** If you don't know the name, take a photo of the bag or box.

Taking herbal medicine with **licorice** (such as jakyakgamcho-tang) for a long time or in large amounts can **raise blood pressure, cause swelling and lower potassium**. Be especially careful if you take blood pressure medicine or diuretics.

Herbal medicine with **ephedra** (such as galgeun-tang and socheongryong-tang) can cause **a pounding heart, trouble sleeping and higher blood pressure**. Ask first if you have heart disease, high blood pressure or an enlarged prostate.
Taking herbal cold medicine with regular cold medicine can **double up similar ingredients** — show both to your pharmacist.
er: **Pounding heart with chest pain or shortness of breath** → **call 119 now**
**Weak, tingling arms and legs with severe swelling** → **see a doctor soon** (licorice may have lowered your potassium)
herb.miss: For granules taken several times a day, take it as soon as you remember, and skip it if the next dose is close. Never a double dose.
